title: Staged auto-adopter for Optimize recommendations with approval gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a safe, auditable, stagewise auto-adopter for Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/caching profiles and lightweight runtime config tweaks). The feature must allow automatic recommendation application with: (1) configurable staged rollout windows, (2) per-canary selection and weight controls, (3) hard safety gates (latency/error/cost thresholds) that trigger immediate rollback, and (4) an approval workflow for optional manual gating.

Scope (in):
- Server-side controller to orchestrate staged rollout of Optimize suggestion artifacts (batching size, prefix cache rules, KV cache TTL hints, quantization profile toggles).
- Canary selection logic based on route, customer tier, and traffic shard.
- Policy engine for safety gates with configurable metrics and thresholds (p95 latency, p99 latency, error-rate, tokens/sec, cost-per-token delta).
- Automatic rollback handler that reverts to last-known-good config and opens an incident/alert.
- Console UI hooks: display staged rollout progress, manual pause/approve/revert buttons, and timeline audit.
- Webhooks/Slack notifications and GitHub PR creation for applied changes (for customers who enable PR flow).

Scope (out):
- Long-lived model-level quantization (requires separate validation and offline benchmarks).
- Deep per-customer policy customizations beyond tier and route.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end test where a suggested batching change is applied to 1% traffic, stepped to 10% after 30m, and stopped at 25% with correct telemetry.
2) Safety gate triggers on simulated 40% p95 increase and automatically rolls back within configured cooldown.
3) Console shows audit trail with timestamps, user/automation actor, and revert button.
4) Slack notification with link to the rollout and the associated GitHub PR is posted on stage transitions and on rollback.
5) Security review completed and feature flags exist to opt-in/out per-organization.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (spike): prototype policy engine and simple controller; produce an integration doc.
- Phase 1: build controller, canary selector, telemetry hooks, and basic rollback action.
- Phase 2: console integration and approval workflow + audit events.
- Phase 3: hardened SLO tests, chaos testing, and customer pilot.

Operational considerations and trade-offs: 
- Trade-off: faster cost savings vs. risk of regressions. Mitigation: short initial canaries, strict default thresholds, opt-in for high-risk customers.
- Trade-off: complexity in selector logic vs. predictability. Mitigation: start with deterministic shard-by-request-hash and route whitelist, later add ML-based selector.

Telemetry & metrics to collect:
- Canary_p95_latency_ms, Canary_p99_latency_ms, Canary_error_rate, Canary_tokens_per_sec, Canary_cost_per_token_delta, Rollout_step_latency_delta, Rollback_time_s, Applied_config_version

Rollout playbook (ops):
- If threshold breach detected: controller pauses, triggers rollback API, posts to #redwood-ops, creates incident with details, and escalates to oncall.
- Manual override: authorized user may resume or force revert via console with reason logged.

APIs and storage:
- New API: POST /optimize-rollouts to start staged adopt (accepts suggestion id, selector, schedule, thresholds, auto_approve boolean).
- Rollout state persisted in rollout-store (schema versioned).

Security & compliance:
- All actions must be logged to audit logs with KMS-encrypted request IDs and user tokens.
- Feature flag per-org default: opt-in for Private deployments; hosted customers default to conservative thresholds.

Deliverables:
- Controller service + feature flag gating.
- Console screens for rollout management and approval.
- Runbook doc and postmortem template.
- Integration tests and two customer pilots.
